data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Append-only identity corruption has two distinct senses that must be separated: (structural) the hash chain is physically broken by a torn write, and (trajectory) the chain is structurally intact but the resumed events belong to a different run trajectory than the committed prefix. A halted run can be resumed without structural corruption iff the tail event is fully committed with a finalized digest (clean halt). It can be resumed without trajectory corruption iff the system's state at the halt point is fully determined by the committed event log, including all non-deterministic inputs. Resumption must be refused for structural corruption (torn write) unconditionally, and for trajectory corruption whenever non-deterministic state was consumed but not logged\u2014even if the chain is structurally perfect.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Structural: the tail event's bytes are incomplete or its digest is not finalized, breaking the chain regardless of trajectory considerations.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Trajectory: the committed events reflect non-deterministic choices (sampling, tool responses) whose state was not persisted, so resumed events cannot follow the original trajectory.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Trajectory: the system's generation state (KV cache, position embeddings, attention window) is not reconstructable from the event log, causing the resumed model to produce different outputs for the same logical context.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Both: a torn write occurs at a point where non-deterministic state was also un-persisted, so neither identity sense is preserved.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Structural identity is a property of the byte sequence and its digest chain: either the bytes form a valid chain or they don't. Trajectory identity is a property of causal continuity: the resumed events must be what the same run would have produced had it not halted. A clean halt preserves structural identity but does not guarantee trajectory identity\u2014if the run called an external tool and recorded only the call but not the response, or sampled from an RNG whose state was not persisted, the resumed events will be structurally valid links but causally alien to the prefix. Thus two independent refusal conditions exist: (1) structural\u2014torn write, broken digest, missing event bytes; (2) trajectory\u2014unlogged non-determinism, unpersisted volatile state, external side effects not replayable from the log. Both must be clean for safe resumption.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
